articles.title: From December 5, businesses may be prohibited from operating during a yellow alert: The Cabinet of Ministers is preparing a postponement until April and June, but not for everyone - Судово-юридична газета

articles.full_text:
20:00, 9 November 2026
3 min
Businesses without shelters may be restricted from operating during air raid alerts starting December 5: the government is working on extending the transition period until April 4, and for certain enterprises — until June 4.
Businesses that do not have shelters or safe spaces may be prohibited from operating during a yellow air raid alert starting December 5. The government proposes to extend the transition period for businesses until April 4, and for certain facilities — until June 4, 2027. However, not everyone will receive a postponement: businesses must document that they began arranging protection before December 4. Moreover, the draft explicitly grants employees the right to refuse dangerous work, and a temporary protected space will not be considered a full substitute for a shelter. What exactly is the Cabinet of Ministers preparing and who will be responsible for people’s safety?
The Ministry of Economy has prepared a draft amendment to Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine resolutions No. 1092 and No. 138, which regulate the operation of enterprises during air raid alerts and the use of civil protection shelters.
The comparative table for the draft confirms that the government proposes not just to extend the deadlines for arranging shelters, but to establish new conditions under which enterprises can operate during a yellow threat level.
The main innovation is that the right to defer will depend on real and documented actions by the business. Enterprises that have not ensured protection for people and have not started relevant measures by December 4 may lose the ability to continue working during the yellow alert level.
At the same time, this is still a draft, not current rules. For the proposed changes to take effect, they must be approved by the Cabinet of Ministers and officially published.
Shelters until April 4 and June 4: who the government wants to extend deadlines for
Cabinet Resolution No. 1092 provided a three-month transition period for enterprises without shelters. Initially, it ends on December 4, 2026.
After appeals from businesses, the government announced preparation of changes to give entrepreneurs additional time.
According to the provided comparative table, two main deadlines are proposed.
Until April 4, 2027, enterprises that have documented the actual start of measures to ensure access to shelters or arrange safe spaces by December 4, 2026, inclusive, will be able to temporarily continue operating during the yellow threat level.
Until June 4, 2027, an extension is foreseen for enterprises that are constructing or reconstructing protective structures or dual-purpose facilities that require project documentation and compliance with legal procedures.
But there is a condition: continuation of work will only be possible if the project’s requirements regarding protection of people are met.
In other words, businesses are not offered unconditional permission to operate until spring or summer 2027. This concerns a transitional regime for those already taking concrete measures.
Meanwhile, the March 4, 2027 date previously mentioned by the Cabinet relates to the collection of information by military administrations about enterprises’ compliance with requirements. It should not be confused with deadlines for completing shelter arrangements.
From December 5, not everyone will be able to work during alerts
The strictest provision of the draft concerns enterprises that do not have shelters and cannot confirm that they have started arranging them.
The proposed version explicitly states: business entities that as of December 4, 2026, have not provided shelters or safe spaces and have not confirmed the start of relevant measures, from December 5 cannot operate during the yellow threat level until the established requirements are met.
This is not a general ban on economic activity nor a requirement to close the enterprise permanently. It concerns specifically the ability to continue working during a yellow air raid alert.
However, for shops, cafes, shopping centers, and other establishments whose activities depend on constant visitor intake, such a norm may have significant economic consequences.
An enterprise that has not yet arranged a shelter but has documented the start of relevant work will have a chance to use the postponement. Businesses that have done nothing will not.
Promises alone are not enough: which documents will save businesses from restrictions
The draft clearly defines how enterprises can confirm the actual start of shelter arrangements.
Possible evidence includes:
- Decisions by the business entity to carry out relevant measures with confirmation of their commencement;
- Documents on technical inspections, assessments of premises, development of technical solutions or project documentation;
- Contracts, orders, payment documents regarding purchase, manufacture, supply, or installation of shelters;
- Documents on preparatory, installation, construction works or reconstruction;
- Confirmation of measures to organize access to already existing protective structures;
- Documents on interaction with owners or custodians of premises or shelters.
The list is not exhaustive.
At the same time, the important factor is not the date of formal document signing, but the ability to confirm specific actions taken before December 4.
One of the most important legal novelties concerns labor rights.
The draft provides that approval to continue work during the yellow threat level will be formalized by a protocol of the general meeting of the labor collective or by written consent of employees involved in the work.
Employees must be informed in advance about existing risks, available shelters, and procedures during air raid alerts.
However, even the consent of the labor collective does not mean the employer has the right to force each employee to continue working under any circumstances.
The draft specifically emphasizes Article 6 of the Law of Ukraine "On Labor Protection." According to it, an employee has the right to refuse assigned work if a production situation arises that is dangerous to their life or health or to people around them, with immediate notification of the direct supervisor or employer.
The employer has no right to force the employee to continue such work.
Thus, the labor collective meeting protocol cannot replace individual labor rights. Moreover, the draft explicitly states that agreement with the collective does not exempt the employer from obligations regarding labor protection and people’s safety.
Two walls instead of a shelter: what the State Emergency Service allows and why it may be insufficient
Alongside preparing regulatory changes, the State Emergency Service (SES) published methodological recommendations on arranging safe spaces.
These can be internal rooms of existing buildings capable of reducing the risk of injury from blast waves and debris.
The service recommends choosing rooms separated from the outside environment by at least two walls, preferably in basements or ground floors.
However, the two-wall rule does not automatically mean the room is suitable.
To assess protective properties, the actual condition of structures, wall and ceiling strength, possible blast wave penetration paths, risk of debris formation, and exit blockages must be considered.
The methodological recommendations include technical guidelines such as:
- Thickness of brick or stone external walls — from 56 cm;
- Internal volume — at least 1.5 cubic meters per person;

articles.full_text:
[Anchor]
Cheating with smart glasses has now been confirmed in middle and high school internal exams, following previous cheating incidents across a wide range of tests, including early college admissions essays, national qualification exams, and official language tests. With the CSAT (College Scholastic Ability Test) fast approaching next week, it looks like a battle against AI glasses.
Reporter Jung Gyeong-yun has the details.
[Reporter]
According to a Ministry of Education investigation, a total of four cases of cheating using AI smart glasses were caught during internal exams at middle and high schools nationwide.
There was 1 case in middle school and 3 cases in high school, and they were identified in various regions across the country, including Seoul, Jeonbuk, and Jeju.
Some students were caught thanks to the sharp eyes of proctors who grew suspicious when students wore unfamiliar glasses and kept touching the frames, while others were exposed when green light reflected off the lenses.
There was also a case where a proctor, having received a tip in advance, watched the student's behavior and caught them.
Students caught using AI glasses receive a score of zero on the respective subject exam.
This is the first time that cheating using AI glasses has been confirmed nationwide in middle and high school exams.
[High School Student: You need to keep up your internal grades, and if the number of students (using AI glasses) increases, I think punishments should also increase. If there could be a device to separately inspect glasses before taking the test....]
[Lee Sun-hee / Policy Director for Middle Schools, Teachers' Union: There is a vague fear of, 'Ah, this is even coming into schools'... After all, you have to suspect your students. There must be a certain level of psychological burden.]
The CSAT is also on high alert.
This is because it can be that much harder for proctors, who usually do not know whether test-takers normally wear glasses, to spot AI glasses.
The Ministry of Education re-emphasized that anyone caught using smart glasses or similar devices will have their CSAT scores nullified this year, be disqualified from taking the test next year, and face criminal punishment, including criminal complaints and police investigations.
Authorities urged students not to bring electronic devices at all, and if they brought them, to make sure to hand them over to the proctor before the start of the first period.
